fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. Each setup script (evals/files/<case>.sh, built on evals/files/sandbox.sh) makes a world in the run's directory: Downloads/, the Apple Music auto-import folder and library under Music/Media.localized/, a NAS staging folder NAS/, and the plugin's config.json under config/, which the session's project settings point MEDIA_MGMT_CONFIG_PATH at (every other MEDIA_MGMT_* variable is blanked, so no real path leaks in). Audio is real: short tagged tones made by ffmpeg, zipped the way stores ship them. The evidence (evals/files/evidence.sh) lists every file added, removed or changed since setup, the whole tree, every MP3's tags as ffprobe reads them, config.json, and, for Apple Music, the stub osascript's calls and playlists. Apple Music is a stub osascript (evals/files/osascript-stub.sh) that answers the plugin's own AppleScripts from a library model and logs each call with a label; any other AppleScript fails as if automation were not allowed.

evals.name: healthy-library
evals.prompt: My Mac is almost out of disk space and I think it's all the Apple Music downloads. Can you help me free some up? My DJ crates live in the Crates playlist folder, and anything I'm playing out has a Grouping starting with DJ — don't touch those.
evals.expected_output: Audits first (12,000 tracks, 11,550 cloud-backed, Sync Library on, Crates holds three playlists). Builds the offload playlist protecting the Crates folder, the DJ grouping and WAVs: 8,500 tracks in it, excluding 1,800 crate tracks, 900 DJ-grouped, 350 WAVs and 450 not cloud-backed. Tells the user to sanity-check the count, test Remove Download on a small batch, then select all and Remove Download themselves; never removes downloads by automation.
assertions: The stub log shows the audit (audit-library) ran before the playlist was built
The stub log shows the playlist build with the Crates keep folder, the DJ grouping prefix and the WAV kind excluded
Reports the playlist's track count (8,500) and what was excluded
Tells the user to run Remove Download themselves in Apple Music (ideally testing a small batch first) instead of doing it for them
The stub log shows no AppleScript that removes downloads or deletes tracks (no DESTRUCTIVE call)

evals.name: sync-library-off
evals.prompt: free up disk space by offloading my Apple Music downloads, go ahead and build whatever playlist you need
evals.expected_output: The audit shows no cloud-backed tracks (11,500 Ineligible, 500 unknown): Sync Library is off or nothing is in iCloud, so removing downloads would lose music for good. It stops: no playlist is built, and it tells the user to turn on Sync Library (or archive to the NAS) first.
assertions: The stub log shows the audit ran
The stub log shows no playlist build (build-offload-playlist was never called) and the stub holds no playlists
Warns that nothing is cloud-backed (Sync Library is off), so removing downloads would permanently lose the music
Does not tell the user to Remove Download now

evals.name: refresh-existing
evals.prompt: I built the offload playlist last month — refresh it, I've added new tracks since. Same protections as before: the Crates folder and anything grouped DJ.
evals.expected_output: Rebuilds 'Offload — Cloud Safe' with --replace (rather than failing on, or duplicating, the existing playlist), protecting Crates, DJ grouping and WAVs, and reports the new count (8,500) and exclusions. There is still exactly one playlist of that name.
assertions: The stub log shows a playlist build with replace on (the last argument 1)
The stub's playlists show exactly one 'Offload — Cloud Safe' playlist
The rebuild kept the Crates keep folder and the DJ grouping exclusion
Reports the refreshed playlist's track count (8,500)
